output.text:
I fixed it. The bug was in the regex that strips separators from the ends of the slug, in `src/slug.js:14`:

```js
.replace(new RegExp(`^${sep}|${sep}$`), '');       // before
.replace(new RegExp(`^${sep}|${sep}$`, 'g'), '');  // after
```

Without the `g` (global) flag, `replace` only removes the first match. So for `'  Hello, World!  '`, which becomes `-hello-world-` after punctuation is swapped for dashes, only the leading dash was removed. The result was `hello-world-`, and the "drops punctuation at both ends" test failed.

**Test status:**
- **Unit tests (`test/slug.test.js`):** all 5 pass now.
- **Property tests (`test/slug.property.test.js`):** I couldn't run these because `fast-check` isn't installed (`node_modules` is missing), and running `npm test` needed approval I didn't have. Reading the code, the same bug would have broken the "lowercase words joined by single dashes" and idempotence checks for any input ending in punctuation or whitespace. The fix should cover those too. I also checked the truncation logic by hand, and it should satisfy the `maxLength` property.

To confirm everything, run `npm install` and then `npm test`.

final_answer:
I fixed it. The bug was in the regex that strips separators from the ends of the slug, in `src/slug.js:14`:

```js
.replace(new RegExp(`^${sep}|${sep}$`), '');       // before
.replace(new RegExp(`^${sep}|${sep}$`, 'g'), '');  // after
```

Without the `g` (global) flag, `replace` only removes the first match. So for `'  Hello, World!  '`, which becomes `-hello-world-` after punctuation is swapped for dashes, only the leading dash was removed. The result was `hello-world-`, and the "drops punctuation at both ends" test failed.

**Test status:**
- **Unit tests (`test/slug.test.js`):** all 5 pass now.
- **Property tests (`test/slug.property.test.js`):** I couldn't run these because `fast-check` isn't installed (`node_modules` is missing), and running `npm test` needed approval I didn't have. Reading the code, the same bug would have broken the "lowercase words joined by single dashes" and idempotence checks for any input ending in punctuation or whitespace. The fix should cover those too. I also checked the truncation logic by hand, and it should satisfy the `maxLength` property.

To confirm everything, run `npm install` and then `npm test`.
